recoveredRecords.title: #40181 - Unlisted biggest variety of Tarnavch coin.
recoveredRecords.description: This variety is unknown even to the authors of newly published book about Chach coins. They detemine metrological data of their type 8, variety 1 as up to 2.5 g and 2.05 cm maximum. This coin is significantly bigger and heavier. However, it is really very rare, the second specimen I heard about and the first in my arms.

recoveredRecords.title: #277703 - Semirech'e, cluster of Anepigraphic AE local imitations
recoveredRecords.description: This is a cluster of very small, thin cast bronze pieces with a holed center. No apparent inscriptions or designs. These seem too small and fragile to have a practical use, and the fact that this group is clustered together may be taken as evidence of hoarding. Very similar to Zeno #243065, also #243067 and #243066. This group sold as part of eBay item #255029261140, 2021. Cf. also https://www.numismall.com/products/w42547?_pos=2&_sid=b1... where similar pieces are described as Kamyshev #32, although I am uncertain whether or not these types are exactly what Kamyshev was describing.

recoveredRecords.title: #128840 - Semirech’e, AE unit
recoveredRecords.description: Unearthed in Kyrgyzstan. 11 dots on obverse, plain caved-in reverse, round hole. Some experts believe this is a degraded imitation of Chinese coins, some believe that it is simply a spare part (spindle) of the utensil (spinner) used for manufacturing of yarn for weaving. Funny thing is that such AE units are unearthed only in Semirech’e. Compare with Zeno ## 128831 , 47785 , 40239 , 128838 .

recoveredRecords.title: #268475 - China, Western Liao, Malik Aram Yinal Qaraj مالك ارام ىىنال قرج, heavy, m/a
recoveredRecords.description: Proto-Qarakhanid, Semirech'ye bronze cash Heavy unworked specimen with hole filled with metal. Compare with Z# 228047 , 228228 , 236091 , 236371 , 256454 and 281281 . Note that their bronzes are different colours. Obv.: Malik Aram Yinal Chig (in Arab.) t-r-b-l Rev.: plain Metal composition of the coin is: Cu 78.41, Zn 7.29, Sn 11.32, As 0.35, Sb 1.16, Pb 0.85, Fe 0.33, Ni 0.18, Co below error level, Sum 99.90%, microprobe data in scanning mode on surface 30x20 mkm. So we have here very low-lead, zincian bronze of yellow colour. Atomic ratio Zn+Fe:Sn ~ 1:1 of the alloy is close to one in mineral kesterite ( https://www.mindat.org/min-2189.html ). Ores with kesterite could to be mined in Zeravshan or Inylchek ranges in Kyrgyzstan. Degradation of the alloy during alteration in ground is typical for bronzes. Leaching of Zn from the coins surface resulted not in redcashization (formation of red copper outer layer) typical for brasses, but silvery-white film of intermetallide Cu2Sn (well visible along the coin edge) was formed. Mineralization crust of the coin is oxide-carbonate type (tenorite + minium -> hydroromarchite -> cerussite) tell us, that the coin initially was burned in open flame and later was oxidized not deep in ground in cold fresh ground water.
